checks.text: The page heading is "Math Editor" and the tab "Source" is selected by default, showing the code area with the placeholder text "Type Markdown and TeX here".

Filling the code area with `# Title`, a blank line, then `Hello $x^2$ world` and waiting for the preview, the tab "Preview" shows an `<h1>` with the text "Title" and a paragraph that contains "Hello", a math element whose accessible name is "x squared", and "world".

Filling the code area with the three lines `| A | B |`, `|---|---|`, `| 1 | 2 |` makes the Preview tab show a table with two column headers ("A" and "B"), two rows in total (one header row, one body row), whose first body cell is "1" and second body cell is "2".

Filling the code area with `- [ ] Task one` and `- [x] Task two` (two lines) makes the Preview tab show a list with two items: the first has an unchecked checkbox and the text "Task one", the second a checked checkbox and the text "Task two".
With the code area containing `# Hi`, a blank line, then `$y$`, clicking the button "Copy Markdown" puts exactly that same text on the clipboard.

With the code area containing `# Hi`, clicking the button "Export HTML" downloads a file named "math-editor.html" whose content includes `

Hi

`.
After filling `# First` and waiting for an autosave, then filling `# Second` and waiting for another autosave, the tab "History" shows two entries: one containing "First" and one containing "Second".
After A7's steps, clicking the button "Restore" in the History entry containing "First" sets the code area to `# First` (Source tab) and the Preview tab shows an `<h1>` with the text "First".
After filling `# Saved Doc` and waiting for autosave, reloading shows the code area containing `# Saved Doc` and the Preview tab showing an `<h1>` with the text "Saved Doc".
